task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a straight news update of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about a new purchase-matching voucher program at Hollowmere Market. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Hollowmere Market Association will launch a grant-funded purchase-matching voucher program on Oct. 10, 2026.
A shopper who spends at least $10 in one qualifying market visit can receive a $5 voucher for a later eligible purchase.
The offer is limited to one voucher per shopper per market day, regardless of how much more than $10 the shopper spends.
The voucher is not cash, carries no cash change and can be used only with participating market traders.
A $20,000 community-commerce grant funds the voucher value, with administration paid separately by the association.
If the entire voucher allocation is issued at $5 each, it can fund 4,000 vouchers; that is capacity, not a reported participation total.
The first round covers produce, bread and pantry ingredients listed in the program rules, not every item sold at the market.
Participating traders will display the association's sign and receive reimbursement for eligible vouchers they submit.
Market coordinator Nella Orr said, "The extra five dollars is a reason to return, not a discount we can claim has already helped every household."
The program is open without an income test and is not part of a government food-benefit system.
The market office will check receipts from the same visit before issuing a voucher, with a staffed alternative for traders using handwritten receipts.
Vouchers issued in the first round must be used by Dec. 19, 2026, the final scheduled market day of that round.
A traders committee asked the association to make reimbursement prompt enough that small stalls are not financing the grant between market days.
Bread seller Paven Rill said, "A token in the till still has to become money we can use to buy flour."
The association plans reimbursements after each market week rather than asking traders to wait until the program ends.
Traders will not be required to participate, and shoppers cannot insist that an unregistered stall accept a voucher.
The association will record issuance and redemption separately because receiving a voucher does not establish that it was later used.
The packet contains no estimate of additional spending, dietary change or household savings produced by the program.
The voucher design includes a serial number and expiry date but does not print the shopper's name.
The market office will display a running notice when the grant allocation is close to being fully issued.
The association has not secured funding for a second round after December.
The market's regular cash and card purchases remain available whether or not a shopper uses the matching offer.

forbidden_additions: An unlimited percentage discount, cash grant or universal trader acceptance.
Four thousand observed users or redemptions.
Government-benefit eligibility rules, measured health outcomes or secured renewal funding.
preserve: The spending threshold, fixed match and per-market-day limit.
Issuance, redemption and trader reimbursement as different events.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
